note: Goal statements and targets are AUTHORED — a commitment cannot be derived. Every current value is MEASURED by hq/server.py's evaluator. A goal nothing can measure says so and counts against this pillar's assurance fraction.

verdict_template.unassured: Nothing here is failing, but {unassured} of {total} of these proofs run on nobody's schedule.
verdict_template.ok: Green on main, and the proofs are fresh enough to believe.

goals.statement: Main is always shippable — the newest finished run of the full suite passed.
goals.statement_short: the newest finished run of the suite failed on main
goals.why_it_matters: Every other proof on this page runs on this machine. This is the one a stranger could check.

path_to_green.narrative: Open the failed run and fix what it caught.

goals.statement: The suite passes almost every time — failures are incidents, not a slow leak.
goals.statement_short: the suite fails often enough to look like a leak rather than an incident
goals.why_it_matters: Three failures in one afternoon is a bad day. Three spread over a month is a test nobody trusts.

path_to_green.narrative: Read the failure ticks on the strip — where they cluster says whether this is one incident or a leak.

goals.statement: Every suite that can be run from this page passed the last time it ran.
goals.statement_short: a suite failed the last time it ran on this machine

path_to_green.narrative: Re-run the failing suite from the buttons below — a loaded machine can skew the benchmark on its own.

goals.statement: Those local proofs were run against something close to what is on main now.
goals.statement_short: the local proofs are stale — they were run many commits ago
goals.why_it_matters: A green verdict from eighty commits ago and one from this commit look identical on a page. Age is the difference between proof and reassurance.

measure.label: how far behind main the local proofs were run

path_to_green.narrative: Run the suites again from the buttons below — from now on each run stamps the commit it proved.

goals.statement: The rules that keep replays reproducible still hold in the code.
goals.statement_short: a rule that keeps replays reproducible is broken in the code
goals.why_it_matters: Recorded sessions are the training data phase 4 runs on. A break here is silent until bot training fails, which is the worst possible time to find out.

members.label: no raw randomness outside the two sanctioned generators
the sim layer touches no node, autoload or input
one gateway for every world mutation
members.reason: Nothing proves every world mutation goes through apply_action. A renderer writing straight into the grid would compile and pass both suites.
members.would_need: A static check over world/, entities/ and player/ for assignments into SimWorld's fields, run as a fifth CI job.

path_to_green.narrative: Two of the three rules are grepped on every page load and hold today. The third has no checker at all; writing one is about half a day.

goals.statement: Recorded sessions can still be tied to the build that produced them.
goals.statement_short: most recorded sessions can no longer be tied to any build
goals.why_it_matters: A session whose build is unresolvable cannot be replayed or scored. It is evidence that has quietly stopped being evidence.

path_to_green.narrative: One fresh session on the tablet from a clean tree fixes this — the same sitting Product needs to close the onboarding gate.
